question: I'm developing a large scale analogue photography project. I want to use films from the Lomography Kino B&W family in 35mm. My lab only has Ilfosol 3 in a 1+9 dilution for the developer. I'll be processing the film at the official box speed and will not be rating the film at a different ISO other than the official one. I'm looking to find out which film takes the least amount of time to develop according to the massive dev chart (using the official box speed only). Since this is such a large scale project, the development time really matters to me so I need to find the film with the lowest development time.

**Film with the shortest official‑speed development time (Ilfosol 3 1 + 9)**  

| Film (Kino B&W – 35 mm) | Official box speed (ASA/ISO) | 35 mm development time – Ilfosol 3 1 + 9 (min) |
|------------------------|-----------------------------|-----------------------------------------------|
| **Lomography Potsdam Kino** | ISO 100 | **6 min** |
| Lomography Berlin Kino | ISO 320 | 6.5 min |
| Lomography Fantôme Kino | ISO 8 | 10.5 min |
| Lomography Babylon Kino | ISO 13 | 12 min |

**Why Potsdam Kino is fastest**

* The **Massive Dev Chart** (DigitalTruth) lists a 35 mm development time of **6 minutes** for Ilfosol 3 at a 1 + 9 dilution when processing Potsdam Kino at its official box speed (ISO 100)【source: Potsdam Kino page】.  
* Berlin Kino, at its official ISO 320, requires 6.5 minutes – longer than Potsdam Kino.  
* The other two family stocks (Fantôme Kino & Babylon Kino) need 10.5 and 12 minutes respectively, both well over Potsdam Kino’s time.  

Therefore, **Lomography Potsdam Kino** gives the shortest uninterrupted development time among the 35 mm Kino B&W films when processed with Ilfosol 3 (1 + 9 dilution) at the official box speed.
